events.summary:
RSVP for the very first meetup of AI for Nonprofits - Portland.

Ninety minutes, and the shape every month after will be the same:

• Short talks (5 minutes): someone shows one thing that actually worked - a prompt that improved a real donor letter, a privacy rule a real board adopted. Real work, shown working. No slides required.

• One deeper conversation: this month - what we're actually using AI for and where we've drawn the line. Small groups, honest notes.

• Field Notes follow up: within two days, everyone gets the write-up from the meetup. Prompts discussed, ideas shared, and more. Lessons travel; names don't.

Bring one thing you've learned, or one thing you're trying to understand.

You do not need to be an AI person.

Free, no vendor pitches, no technical background needed.
We wrap at 12:30 - conversations that want to keep going can move out to Pioneer Courthouse Square.

Questions, or something you'd like presented for you (anonymously is fine): weston@tomorrowlabs.org

This event will be co-hosted by Weston Cox (TomorrowLabs) and Surj (PunkWorks) - both human-centered technologists with experience in nonprofits and mission-driven organizations.
events.title: Ai for Nonprofits - Portland

Summary:

Russell will talk about OpenWrt on Realtek-based switches, like the EnGenius EWS2910P and Zyxel GS1900 line of managed switches. Some devices provide Power over Ethernet with port-level control. The talk will include some fun demonstrations of installation and reverse engineering.

Bio:

Russell has been a Linux user since December 1992.  Since 2005, he's been involved with the Personal Telco Project, and has been the President of that organization since 2009, building public-access wifi networks and advocating for better telecommunications policy. He's also been active in an effort to energize political support for a public fiber-optic last-mile network in Portland in order to break the monopoly power of the deregulated incumbent carriers. In recent years, he's become more active in recruiting speakers for PLUG, kind of accidentally falling into the coordinator role as Michael Dexter stepped back. This talk represents a failure to find a better speaker, not only Russell's failure, but the failure of the entire PLUG community. Shame on one and all! ;-)
events.title: Portland Linux/Unix Group General Monthly Meeting: Installing OpenWrt on Realtek-based managed switches, with Russell Senior

- Open conversation: no slides, no sales pitch.

- Small‑group or one‑on‑one discussions: get your questions answered.

📍 Upper Left Roasters ([1204 SE Clay St, Portland, OR 97214](https://maps.app.goo.gl/LW7B2gDtSuWTVuvJ8))

🗓 August 12, 2026 from 11am-2pm ([Add to Calendar](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/event?action=TEMPLATE&tmeid=NnQ1cDJhZGl2cHQ4ZGd1MnVubXZiM3ZwY2wgY19iMWMwNzI1YjNjNjQzYjRiNWUzNWZhNTAyYjAwYzU5MzUwOTNiYTU5ZmI5MmUxYzdmNTg4Y2Q2ODhhODgzZGViQGc&tmsrc=c_b1c0725b3c643b4b5e35fa502b00c5935093ba59fb92e1c7f588cd688a883deb%40group.calendar.google.com))

💲 Free

Bring your questions, leave with new insights and a clearer understanding of AI’s possibilities.

**About Leila:**

[Leila Kaneda (she/her)](https://www.linkedin.com/in/leilahawana/) is an experienced machine learning strategist, researcher, engineer, and founder with a passion for helping organizations harness AI to solve real-world problems. She holds a masters degree in AI and has spent a decade building production-grade ML systems across a variety of different industries such as nonprofits, restaurants, retail, agriculture, aerospace, finance, semiconductor, sustainability, and more. She has also spent more than 20 years as an educator, including some time as an adjunct instructor at Portland State University. 

Leila is known for her ability to translate complex machine learning concepts into clear, actionable strategies that empower teams and drive innovation. Beyond her technical work, she’s an active speaker, educator, and community leader dedicated to making cutting-edge technology accessible and impactful.

Join us for a Virtual Lunch & Learn presented by Oliver Richards and Madelyn McCormick as they explore the common patent mistakes that early-stage companies make and how to avoid costly issues down the road. Most patent mistakes are cheap to avoid and expensive to fix. The trouble is that the fixing usually happens years later, in a licensing dispute, a due-diligence review, or a courtroom, long after the startup that made the mistake has moved on. This session looks at the most common patent errors early-stage companies make, from public disclosures that quietly forfeit foreign rights, to ownership and inventorship gaps, to provisional applications that don’t actually protect what the founders think they do.

Rather than a checklist of best practices, the talk works backward from how these mistakes surface once a patent is challenged or enforced, from the vantage point of a patent litigator who spends his days on the consequences. Attendees will leave with a practical sense of which early decisions actually matter, which ones are recoverable, and where a modest investment of attention up front saves a great deal of money and heartburn later.
events.title: Virtual Lunch & Learn: Patent Pitfalls: The Early Mistakes That Come Back to Bite You

AI isn't just something UX designers design for -- it's something we can design with. In this talk, Rikki will share how she has integrated AI tools into her own UX practice to produce higher-quality work, faster.

From generating working prototypes instead of static mockups, to using AI as a thinking partner during research synthesis, to building complete products as a solo designer -- Rikki will show real examples of how AI collapses the gap between "design intent" and "working thing." This isn't about replacing craft. It's about raising the bar on what one designer can ship.

For September, we're taking advantage of a speaker in town for DevOpsDaysPDX, and making it an all-observability night, with FluentBit and OpenTelemetry.

Date: Wednesday, September 16, 2026
Time: 6:00 PM – 8:00 PM
Location: SteepleJack Brewing, Fireside Room, 2400 NE Broadway, Portland

Talks are typically recorded (opt-in by speakers)

A big thank you to SuSE for sponsoring catering at SteepleJack, as well as Eric's travel.

First Presentation: No C, No Opaque AI: Watch Your First Fluent Bit Contribution Happen Live

Speaker: Eric D. Schabell, SuSE

Contributing to a CNCF graduated project feels out of reach until someone shows you exactly how it happens. In this session, that someone is on stage doing it in real time — spotting a gap between what the Fluent Bit codebase actually does and what the docs say, opening a branch on a live fork, running the project's prose linter, writing a properly signed commit, and pushing a pull request that closes a real tracked issue. Every step, no shortcuts, no slides pretending to be a terminal.

You will leave knowing the two-repo mental model that makes Fluent Bit doc contributions work, the git habits that signal credibility to maintainers, and the AI guardrails that keep your name attached to work you actually stand behind. Your first PR does not require deep C knowledge. It requires knowing where to look, how to show your work, and when to keep your hands on the wheel."

Second Presentation: Devs, Transform (Your Data) and Roll Out!: Learning and Leveraging OTTL

Speaker: Reese Lee, New Relic

The OpenTelemetry Collector is OTel’s power tool for ingesting and processing your app and infrastructure data, but there’s even more you can do with your data before it reaches your backend! Learn how to start leveraging OTTL, or OpenTelemetry Transformation Language, to manage your data volume and quality. We’ll explore the syntax basics and its underlying architecture within the Collector, where its strength really comes into play, when to use it (or not!), and more.
events.title: Cloud Native PDX September: Observability Night!
